newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Discount offering to include shares.
newsitem.headline: Discount offering to include shares.

text.p: The Israeli government's offering of Israel Discount Bank will include shares and two series of warrants, the Treasury said in a letter to the parliamentary finance committee released on Tuesday.

Finance Minister Dan Meridor said the secondary offering for 17 percent of Discount would include shares and warrants to be excercised three and nine months after the offering date. He estimated the offering would raise about 600 million shekels.

Meridor said the share tranche would be about 28 percent of the total proceeds, the three-month warrants 32 percent and the nine-month options the remainder. The offering is expected to be made later this month.

Institutional investors will be entitled to bid prior to the public offering for 60 percent of the issue. Discount's employees will also be entitled to shares equal to 10 percent of the public offering.

The government floated 14.5 percent of Discount, Israel's third-largest commercial bank, in March 1996. The bank's shares had been removed from trading on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange after the government took the bank over in the wake of the 1983 bank shares crash.
Market sources had said the government had planned to make an offering of warrants only, which they said would have discouraged foreign participation in the offering.
